stepNotes.1: A four-function Env namespace wraps an Instance-owned snapshot copied from process.env.
stepNotes.2: Environment secrets and routing values stay instance-local, but callers must not mistake set() for a process.env mutation.
stepNotes.3: All accessors share one per-instance object; all() exposes that object by reference and makes direct mutation part of the effective contract.
stepNotes.4: Only the initial O(environment keys) copy has material cost; steady-state operations are property access with no growing cache.
stepNotes.5: Delegating context lifetime to Instance is clean, while the mutable all() result deserves explicit documentation or stronger typing.
stepNotes.6: The implementation contains no TODOs, empty catches, unused helpers, or unreachable branches.
stepNotes.7: Both audit-listed env tests target other environment helpers, leaving this namespace without direct snapshot or mutation coverage.
stepNotes.8: No accepted finding exists; mutable exposure and absent unit tests remain design/test-gap observations only.
stepNotes.9: Core typechecking passed; a new direct Env test is the meaningful next verification command.
